item.name: 00. What's New — Phone & Laptop Models and Specs
item.description:
Everything the app needs for **phone & laptop models**, **phone specs (RAM, storage)** and **laptop specs**, in the order you'd build it. These are copies of requests that also live in the numbered folders below; nothing else changed.

## What's new
- **Models** — Mobile Phones and Laptops & Computers brands now have models (Apple → iPhone 6 … iPhone 17 Pro Max; HP → EliteBook, ProBook, …). Sellers pick one when posting; buyers browse and filter by it.
- **Laptop specs** — Laptops & Computers ads carry `processor`, `ram`, `storage` and `storage_type`, chosen from fixed lists.
- **Phone specs** — Mobile Phones ads carry `ram` and `storage`, chosen from fixed lists (sent as `phone_ram` / `phone_storage`). Existing ads have been filled in from their titles and descriptions; most phones have storage, and about 1 in 6 has RAM (iPhone sellers rarely give it).
- **Model pages** — every model has its own page of ads (e.g. Apple iPhone 12 Pro Max).

## Build order
1. **Post & edit** — show a Model dropdown after the brand, plus optional RAM / Storage dropdowns for phones and the spec dropdowns for laptops, then send `model` and the specs with create/update.
2. **Browse** — show a brand's models on the brand page, open a model page, and show model & specs on the ad.
3. **Filter** — add Model (phones & laptops), Storage / RAM (phones) and Processor / RAM / Storage (laptops) to the filter sheet. All spec lists come from `GET /api/search/filters`.

## IDs (production)
| | Category | Subcategory |
|---|---|---|
| Mobile Phones | 4 `mobile-phones-and-tablets` | 6 `mobile-phones` |
| Laptops & Computers | 2 `electronics` | 27 `laptops-computers` |

**Phone brands:** Apple 1542 · Samsung 13 · Tecno 1541 · Infinix 15 · Xiaomi 1540 · Itel 1581
**Laptop brands:** HP 4851 · Dell 4852 · Lenovo 4853 · Apple 4854 · Asus 4855 · Acer 4856 · Microsoft 4857 · Toshiba 4858 · Samsung 4859 · MSI 4860 · Huawei 4861

Model IDs differ per brand and can grow — always load them from `GET /api/adverts/brands/{brandId}/models` rather than hard-coding them.

## Phone spec values
Load these from `phone_specs` in `GET /api/search/filters` (or `phone_spec_options` in `GET /api/adverts/create/data`); current values:
- **phone_ram:** 1GB, 2GB, 3GB, 4GB, 6GB, 8GB, 12GB, 16GB, 24GB
- **phone_storage:** 8GB, 16GB, 32GB, 64GB, 128GB, 256GB, 512GB, 1TB, 2TB

## Laptop spec values
Load these from `computer_specs` in `GET /api/search/filters` (or `computer_options` in `GET /api/adverts/create/data`); current values:
- **processor:** Intel Core i3, Intel Core i5, Intel Core i7, Intel Core i9, Intel Core Ultra 5, Intel Core Ultra 7, Intel Core Ultra 9, Intel Celeron, Intel Pentium, Intel Core M, Intel Core 2 Duo, Intel Xeon, AMD Ryzen 3, AMD Ryzen 5, AMD Ryzen 7, AMD Ryzen 9, AMD A-Series, AMD Athlon, Apple M1, Apple M2, Apple M3, Apple M4, Other
- **ram:** 2GB, 4GB, 6GB, 8GB, 12GB, 16GB, 24GB, 32GB, 48GB, 64GB
- **storage:** 16GB, 32GB, 64GB, 128GB, 256GB, 320GB, 500GB, 512GB, 750GB, 1TB, 2TB
- **storage_type:** SSD, HDD, SSD + HDD, eMMC

## Changed responses (existing endpoints)
- `GET /api/adverts/{id}` → `model`, `computer` for laptops, and `ram` / `storage` in `phone` for phones
- `GET /api/adverts/create/data` → `computer_options`, `phone_spec_options`
- `GET /api/adverts/{id}/edit` → `models`, `model_field`, `advert.computer`
- `GET /api/brands/{cat}/{sub}/{brand}` → `models[]` with `advert_count`
- `GET /api/user/wishlist` → `computer` on each item; `phone` now includes `ram` / `storage`
- `POST /api/search/filter` → accepts `model`, `processor`, `ram`, `storage`, `phone_ram`, `phone_storage`
- `GET /api/search/filters` → `phone_specs`, `computer_specs`
- `POST /api/adverts`, `PUT /api/adverts/{id}` → accept `phone_ram`, `phone_storage`

request.description:
After the seller picks a brand, call this to fill the **Model** dropdown. Append `model_field.other_option` as the last option.

_Copy of **02. Adverts → Get Models by Brand**; the full reference is there._

---

🌐 **Public Endpoint**

Endpoint: `GET /api/adverts/brands/{brandId}/models`
Controller: `App\Http\Controllers\Api\UserManageAdverts@fetchModels`

Models for a brand, in release order (Apple: iPhone 6 → iPhone 17 Pro Max; HP: EliteBook, ProBook, …). Use it to fill the Model dropdown on the post/edit advert screens.

**`model_field`** tells the app how to render the dropdown:
- `show` — show the Model field (the brand has models)
- `required` — the web forms require it; the API itself still accepts a missing model and infers one from the title
- `other_option` — Mobile Phones and Laptops & Computers: append this as the last option (`value: "other"`, label "Other / not listed") so a seller whose phone/laptop isn't listed can still post. It is stored as no model.

**Phone models (iPhone 11, 12 Pro Max, …):** models live in the same `models` table as car models, keyed by brand (Apple = 1542). A phone advert's model is stored in `phone_details.model`; a car's in `car_details.model`.

**Laptops & Computers (`subcategory` 27):** works the same as phones. Brands are makers (HP, Dell, Lenovo, Apple, …) and models are product lines (EliteBook, Latitude, ThinkPad, MacBook Pro, …). Send `model` as an ID from `GET /api/adverts/brands/{brand}/models`, or `"other"`. If it's omitted, the model is inferred from `ad_title` ("HP Elitebook 840 G5" → EliteBook). It is stored in `computer_details.model`, and the advert's `computer` relation is returned alongside `car` / `phone`.

item.name: 3a. Create ad — phone with model, RAM & storage

request.description:
Phone ad with `model` = iPhone 12 Pro Max (3568). Send `"other"` when the phone isn't listed, or leave `model` out to have it read from the title.

_Copy of **06. User Manage Adverts (Protected) → Create New Advert**; the full reference is there._

---

🔒 **Requires Authentication**\n\nEndpoint: `POST /api/adverts`\nController: `App\Http\Controllers\Api\UserManageAdverts@createAdvert`\n\nCreate a new advert with images and details

**Phone models (Mobile Phones, `subcategory` 6):**
- `model` — a model ID from `GET /api/adverts/brands/{brand}/models`, or `"other"` when the phone isn't listed (stored as no model).
- Optional on the API: if omitted, the model is inferred from `ad_title` (e.g. "UK used iPhone 13 Pro Max" → iPhone 13 Pro Max). Titles that name several models, or none, are stored without a model.
- A model ID that doesn't belong to the brand → `422 {"errors": {"model": ["The selected model is invalid."]}}`.

**Laptops & Computers (`subcategory` 27):** works the same as phones. Brands are makers (HP, Dell, Lenovo, Apple, …) and models are product lines (EliteBook, Latitude, ThinkPad, MacBook Pro, …). Send `model` as an ID from `GET /api/adverts/brands/{brand}/models`, or `"other"`. If it's omitted, the model is inferred from `ad_title` ("HP Elitebook 840 G5" → EliteBook). It is stored in `computer_details.model`, and the advert's `computer` relation is returned alongside `car` / `phone`.

**Laptop specs (`subcategory` 27, all optional):** `processor`, `ram`, `storage`, `storage_type` — values from `data.computer_options` in `GET /api/adverts/create/data` (e.g. `Intel Core i5`, `8GB`, `256GB`, `SSD`). Any spec not sent is read from `ad_title` + `description` ("Core i5 8GB RAM 256GB SSD"); an unlisted value fails validation. Stored on `computer_details` and returned in the `computer` relation.

**Phone specs (Mobile Phones, `subcategory` 6, both optional):** `phone_ram`, `phone_storage` — values from `data.phone_spec_options` in `GET /api/adverts/create/data` (also `data.phone_specs` in `GET /api/search/filters`), e.g. `8GB`, `256GB`. They're prefixed with `phone_` because `ram` / `storage` are the laptop fields. A spec left blank is read from `ad_title` + `description` ("8gb ram 256gb rom", "iPhone 12 128GB"); an unlisted value fails validation (`422`). On update, a spec not sent at all keeps its saved value. Stored on `phone_details` and returned in the `phone` relation as `ram` / `storage`.

**Laptop specs (`subcategory` 27, all optional):** `processor`, `ram`, `storage`, `storage_type` — values from `data.computer_options` in `GET /api/adverts/create/data` (e.g. `Intel Core i5`, `8GB`, `256GB`, `SSD`). On update, specs not sent keep their current value (or, if empty, are read from `ad_title` + `description` ("Core i5 8GB RAM 256GB SSD")); an unlisted value fails validation. Stored on `computer_details` and returned in the `computer` relation.

**Phone specs (Mobile Phones, `subcategory` 6, both optional):** `phone_ram`, `phone_storage` — values from `data.phone_spec_options` in `GET /api/adverts/create/data` (also `data.phone_specs` in `GET /api/search/filters`), e.g. `8GB`, `256GB`. They're prefixed with `phone_` because `ram` / `storage` are the laptop fields. A spec left blank is read from `ad_title` + `description` ("8gb ram 256gb rom", "iPhone 12 128GB"); an unlisted value fails validation (`422`). On update, a spec not sent at all keeps its saved value. Stored on `phone_details` and returned in the `phone` relation as `ram` / `storage`.

Pass `brand` to get `data.models` for the filter sheet. `data.phone_specs` and `data.computer_specs` hold the RAM / Storage (phones) and Processor / RAM / Storage (laptops) choices.

_Copy of **04. Search → Search Filters**; the full reference is there._

---

Endpoint: `GET /api/search/filters`
Controller: `App\Http\Controllers\Api\SearchController@getFilters`

Filter options for the search screen: categories, states, price ranges, seller types, conditions.

**Query Params:**
- `brand` (integer, optional) — also return `data.models`: the brand's models with active ads, most-listed first, each with `advert_count` (phones, laptops and cars — e.g. `brand=13` Samsung, `brand=4851` HP). Send the selected IDs back as `model` to `POST /api/search/filter`.

**Spec lists for the filter sheet:**
- `data.phone_specs` — `{ram: [...], storage: [...]}` for Mobile Phones; send the chosen values as `phone_ram` / `phone_storage` to `POST /api/search/filter`.
- `data.computer_specs` — `{processor: [...], ram: [...], storage: [...], storage_type: [...]}` for Laptops & Computers; send them as `processor` / `ram` / `storage`.

🌐 **Public Endpoint**

Endpoint: `GET /api/adverts/brands/{brandId}/models`
Controller: `App\Http\Controllers\Api\UserManageAdverts@fetchModels`

Models for a brand, in release order (Apple: iPhone 6 → iPhone 17 Pro Max; HP: EliteBook, ProBook, …). Use it to fill the Model dropdown on the post/edit advert screens.

**`model_field`** tells the app how to render the dropdown:
- `show` — show the Model field (the brand has models)
- `required` — the web forms require it; the API itself still accepts a missing model and infers one from the title
- `other_option` — Mobile Phones and Laptops & Computers: append this as the last option (`value: "other"`, label "Other / not listed") so a seller whose phone/laptop isn't listed can still post. It is stored as no model.

**Phone models (iPhone 11, 12 Pro Max, …):** models live in the same `models` table as car models, keyed by brand (Apple = 1542). A phone advert's model is stored in `phone_details.model`; a car's in `car_details.model`.

**Laptops & Computers (`subcategory` 27):** works the same as phones. Brands are makers (HP, Dell, Lenovo, Apple, …) and models are product lines (EliteBook, Latitude, ThinkPad, MacBook Pro, …). Send `model` as an ID from `GET /api/adverts/brands/{brand}/models`, or `"other"`. If it's omitted, the model is inferred from `ad_title` ("HP Elitebook 840 G5" → EliteBook). It is stored in `computer_details.model`, and the advert's `computer` relation is returned alongside `car` / `phone`.

**Brands with models** (production IDs):

| Subcategory | Brand (ID) | Models | e.g. |
|---|---|---|---|
| Mobile Phones (6) | Samsung (13) | 95 | Galaxy S24, Galaxy A14, Galaxy Z Fold 4 |
| Mobile Phones (6) | Tecno (1541) | 63 | Camon 20, Spark 10, Pop 10 |

| Mobile Phones (6) | Apple (1542) | 41 | iPhone XR, iPhone 12 Pro Max |
| Mobile Phones (6) | Itel (1581) | 12 | A70, P55, S25 Ultra |
| Laptops & Computers (27) | HP (4851) | 13 | EliteBook, ProBook, Pavilion |
| Laptops & Computers (27) | Dell (4852) | 8 | Latitude, Inspiron, XPS |
| Laptops & Computers (27) | Lenovo (4853) | 8 | ThinkPad, IdeaPad, Yoga |
| Laptops & Computers (27) | MSI (4860) | 8 | Katana, Modern, GF63 |
| Laptops & Computers (27) | Acer (4856) | 7 | Aspire, Swift, TravelMate |
| Laptops & Computers (27) | Asus (4855) | 6 | VivoBook, ZenBook, ROG |
| Laptops & Computers (27) | Apple (4854) | 5 | MacBook, MacBook Air, MacBook Pro |

Don't hard-code this list: any brand whose `GET /api/adverts/brands/{brandId}/models` returns models (`model_field.show: true`) works the same way. Brands without models (e.g. Nokia, or "Other") return an empty list and `model_field.show: false` — hide the Model field.

request.description:
🌐 **Public Endpoint — laptop model page (e.g. "HP EliteBook")**

Same as *Brand Model Adverts*, for Laptops & Computers. Web equivalent: `/category/electronics/laptops-computers/hp-laptops-computers/hp-elitebook`.

Each ad's model and specs are in `computer` on `GET /api/adverts/{id}`. Narrow further with `POST /api/search/filter` (`brand`, `model`, `processor`, `ram`, `storage`).

🌐 **Public Endpoint**

Endpoint: `POST /api/search`
Controller: `App\Http\Controllers\Api\SearchController@search`

**Request Body:**
- `product` (string, optional, min 3 chars): Search term
- `location` (string, optional): State name (e.g. `Addis Ababa`)
- `category` (integer, optional): Category ID
- `sub_category` (integer, optional): Sub-category ID
- `brand` (integer, optional): Brand ID
- `buydirect` (string, optional): `yes` or `no`
- `item_condition` (string, optional): See condition values below
- `per_page` (integer, optional, default 20)
- `page` (integer, optional, default 1)

**`item_condition` values:**
- General categories: `New`, `Foreign Used`, `Locally Used`
- Vehicles (category 1): `Local used`, `Foreign used`
- Phones & Tablets (category 4): `New - Unboxed`, `New - No Packaging`, `Used - Very Good`, `Used - Good`, `Used - Defect`, `Foreign Used - No Packaging`

> The correct table is chosen automatically based on `category`.

🌐 **Public Endpoint — Unified Filter (replaces all filter-by-* endpoints)**

Endpoint: `POST /api/search/filter`
Controller: `App\Http\Controllers\Api\SearchController@filter`

All parameters are optional. Pass only the ones you need. Car/phone detail joins only activate when their specific params are present.

**General Parameters:**
- `keyword` (string, optional) — search term, matches ad title or ad_id
- `category` (integer, optional) — Category ID
- `sub_category` (integer, optional) — Sub-category ID
- `brand` (integer, optional) — Brand ID
- `location` (string, optional) — State name e.g. `Addis Ababa`
- `per_page` (integer, optional, default 20)
- `page` (integer, optional, default 1)

**Price Parameters** (use `min`/`max` OR `range`, not both):
- `min` (integer, optional) — minimum price
- `max` (integer, optional) — maximum price
- `range` (string, optional) — `under_20k` \| `20k_120k` \| `120k_1m` \| `1m_10m` \| `above_10m`

**Listing Type Parameters:**
- `buydirect` (string, optional) — `Yes` or `No`
- `seller` (string, optional) — `all` \| `verified` \| `unverified`
- `item_condition` (string, optional) — general condition for non-car, non-phone categories: `New` \| `Foreign Used` \| `Locally Used`

**Vehicle-Specific Parameters** (category 1 — Vehicles):
- `car_condition` (string or array, optional) — `Local used` \| `Foreign used`
- `fuel_type` (string or array, optional) — `Petrol` \| `Diesel` \| `Electric` \| `Hybrid` \| `Natural gas CNG` \| `LPG`
- `transmission` (string or array, optional) — `Automatic` \| `Manual` \| `AMT` \| `CVT`
- `registration` (string or array, optional) — `Registered` \| `Unregistered`

**Phone-Specific Parameters** (category 4 — Mobile Phones & Tablets):
- `phone_condition` (string or array, optional) — `New - Unboxed` \| `New - No Packaging` \| `Used - Very Good` \| `Used - Good` \| `Used - Defect` \| `Foreign Used - No Packaging`
- `device_type` (string or array, optional) — `Smartphone` \| `Feature Phone` \| `Tablet`

**Response includes `filters_applied`** — echoes back only the filters that were active in the query.

> The old endpoints (`filter-by-seller`, `filter-by-buydirect`, `filter-by-car`, `filter-by-phone`) still work for backward compatibility but this single endpoint should be used for all new development.

🌐 **Public Endpoint** (no auth required)

Endpoint: `GET /api/adverts/image-requirements`
Controller: `App\Http\Controllers\Api\UserManageAdverts@imageRequirements`

Returns the admin-configured image requirements (count, dimensions, file size, format) that the server enforces when creating/updating an advert. Cached ~1hr server-side per setting; safe for the client to cache too.

The same object is also embedded under `data.image_requirements` in `GET /api/adverts/create/data`.

**Field reference:**
- `min_images` / `max_images` — number of images required/allowed per advert (not applied to Jobs/CV categories)
- `min_width` / `min_height` — images below this resolution are rejected
- `recommended_width` / `recommended_height` — images below this (but above the minimum) are accepted with a quality warning
- `min_file_size_bytes` / `max_file_size_bytes` — file size bounds in bytes
- `max_file_size_kb` — same max, in kilobytes
- `allowed_formats` — accepted image mime subtypes
- `strictness` — 1–10, how strictly the server's own quality checks (blur, brightness, overall score) are applied; informational, not something the client needs to replicate

**Mobile Implementation:**
1. Fetch on "Post Ad" screen load (or reuse the value already returned by `create/data`)
2. Validate images client-side against these numbers before upload — count, resolution, file size — and show one clear message per rule
3. Don't hardcode these numbers; they change whenever the admin updates settings
4. The server still re-validates on upload/create — this endpoint lets the client match those rules, it doesn't replace server-side enforcement

request.description:
🔒 **Requires Authentication (Buyer only)**

Endpoint: `POST /api/user/payments/{paymentId}/resume`
Controller: `App\Http\Controllers\Api\UserController@resumePayment`

Mobile equivalent of the web **Complete Payment** button on My Orders. Re-initializes a Flutterwave transaction for an abandoned (pending) payment and returns a fresh `authorization_url`.

**URL Parameter:**
- `paymentId` — The payment record `id` (integer). Get this from the pending orders list.

**No request body required.**

**Mobile flow:**
1. Show pending orders (payments with `payment_status = pending`)
2. User taps **Complete Payment** → call this endpoint
3. On success, open `authorization_url` in an in-app browser / WebView
4. Flutterwave calls the callback URL after payment — order is marked paid automatically
5. Redirect user back to My Orders screen

**Authorization:**
- Returns `404` if the payment does not belong to the authenticated user or is not pending
- Returns `409` if the ad has already been sold to another buyer
- Returns `502` if Flutterwave fails to initialize
